gifCompress.title: GIF Compressor · Toolbox
gifCompress.description: Compress GIFs right in your browser: automatically steps through scale + frame-skipping + palette quantization (with dithering) combos and picks the first plan that meets the target size with the highest quality. Files never leave your device.
gifCompress.heading: GIF Compressor
gifCompress.introRich: Upload a .gif animation and the tool automatically steps through scale + frame-skipping + palette quantization combos, picking the first plan that meets the target size with the highest quality while keeping total playback duration unchanged. Everything runs locally in your browser — files are never uploaded to any server.
gifCompress.invalidGif: This file does not look like a valid GIF (the header should be GIF87a / GIF89a).
gifCompress.readUnknownError: An unknown error occurred while reading the file.
gifCompress.progressText: Pass {attempt}/{total} · scale {scale}% · 1 of every {step} frames · {colors} colors · frame {frame}/{totalFrames}
gifCompress.doneNotMet: Compressed with the most aggressive settings, but the target size was not reached — see the result on the right.
gifCompress.compressUnknownError: An unknown error occurred during compression.
gifCompress.dropHint: Click to choose, or drop a .gif file here
gifCompress.ditherDesc: Uses error diffusion to simulate gradients when reducing colors — fewer bands and a smoother look, at the cost of slightly slower processing and a bit more size.
gifCompress.notMetHint: Even the most aggressive settings could not reach the target — try a larger target size.
gifCompress.downloadNote: The original file stays untouched; the compressed version is saved as a new file.
gifCompress.note1Rich: Everything runs locally in your browser — files are never uploaded to any server.
gifCompress.note2Rich: Delays of dropped frames are proportionally added to the kept frames, so total duration and pacing stay the same.
gifCompress.note3: GIFs with many frames or large dimensions need several passes — please be patient.
gifCompress.note4: If the result looks too small or lacks color, try again with a larger target size.
gifCompress.emptyResult: The compressed GIF will appear here
gifCompress.principleRich: Tries scale + frame-skipping + palette quantization combos from highest to lowest quality and picks the first plan that meets the target size. Decoding uses gifuct-js, quantization and encoding use gifenc, and dithering is Floyd–Steinberg error diffusion — equivalent to the classic Python + Pillow approach.

swfToExe.title: SWF to EXE · Toolbox
swfToExe.description: Package a Flash animation / game (.swf) into a standalone Windows player (.exe) right in your browser. Files never leave your device.
swfToExe.heading: SWF to EXE
swfToExe.introRich: Upload a .swf file and bundle it with the standalone Flash projector into a double-clickable .exe program. Everything runs locally in your browser — files are never uploaded to any server.
swfToExe.invalidSwf: This file does not look like a valid SWF (the header should be FWS / CWS / ZWS).
swfToExe.customProjectorMissing: You chose to use a custom projector — please select a Flash projector .exe file first.
swfToExe.bundledProjectorFailed: Failed to load the bundled projector ({status})
swfToExe.invalidProjector: The projector file does not look like a valid Windows executable (missing MZ header).
swfToExe.packUnknownError: An unknown error occurred while packaging.
swfToExe.dropHint: Click to choose, or drop a .swf file here
swfToExe.bundledDesc: A clean standalone Flash projector is bundled with this site — ready to use out of the box.
swfToExe.customDesc: Bring your own Flash Player standalone projector .exe.
swfToExe.unzipHint: Unzip and double-click the .exe inside to play.
swfToExe.emptyResult: The generated ZIP will appear here
swfToExe.note1Rich: To avoid browsers blocking EXE downloads, the output is delivered as a ZIP archive — unzip it and double-click the .exe inside.
swfToExe.note2Rich: The generated program is a Windows executable and only runs on Windows.
swfToExe.note3Rich: Everything runs locally in your browser — files are never uploaded to any server.
swfToExe.note4Rich: The Flash player is embedded in the output — just double-click to run, no Flash installation needed.
swfToExe.note5: If antivirus / SmartScreen blocks the first run, choose “Run anyway” — a common false positive for self-extracting programs.
swfToExe.principleRich: The standalone Flash projector looks for a special footer at the end of its own file. This tool appends your SWF to the projector and writes the 0xFA123456 magic number plus the file length. When the projector starts and finds this footer, it loads and plays the embedded SWF.

about.title: About
about.metaDescription: Data sources, methodology and credits for this World Cup history database. Data from the Fjelstul World Cup Database, licensed CC-BY-SA 4.0.
about.heading: About this database
about.intro: A read-only, static, data-only archive of the men's World Cup. Every page is computed once at build time — nothing is calculated while you browse.
about.sourcesRich: All data comes from Joshua C. Fjelstul's <db>The Fjelstul World Cup Database v.1.2.0</db> (2023), used under the <cc>CC-BY-SA 4.0</cc> license. You may freely download and redistribute the data with attribution, under the same license.
about.method1: · Men's World Cup only (1930–2022): 22 tournaments, 964 matches, 2,720 goals.
about.method2: · Defunct or renamed national teams (Soviet Union SUN, Yugoslavia YUG, Czechoslovakia CSK, West Germany FRG, East Germany DDR, etc.) are counted separately under their historical identities, never merged with successor states — hence 85 teams.
about.method3: · Lineups, substitutions and cards are officially recorded only from 1970 onwards; earlier matches keep basic data such as goals.
about.method4: · Three-letter country codes follow the football coding of the Fjelstul database (Saudi Arabia SAU, Ivory Coast CIV, etc.).
about.method5: · This site contains no win-probability models or ELO ratings — only historical facts.
about.namesText: Player, manager and referee names keep their original Latin spelling (Pelé, Maradona); team and stage names are localized.

match.noLineups: FIFA match reports only include lineups, substitutions and cards from 1970 onwards; this is an early match, so only the goal record survives.
